summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module 38.1.7 ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and execFileSyncs it against a bundled math_init.js file at the tarball root. math_init.js is a single-line 727KB blob obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style shuffled string/char-code table and a runtime decoder — its behavior is intentionally opaque and executes during `npm install`. The main entry dist/index.js is unrelated React 'lazyModule' code, and neither the Bun runtime nor a 'math init' step has any relationship to the advertised Suspense-wrapper library. The tarball's declared manifest lists `"files": ["dist", "src"]`, so setup.mjs and math_init.js are smuggled outside the declared publish surface, while package.json claims the ServiceTitan uikit homepage and repository — an identity/contents mismatch consistent with a compromised or impersonating publish of the legitimate @servicetitan scope. Fetching a second-language runtime at install time and using it to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled payload is an alternate-runtime dropper: it delivers code execution on the installer's machine while evading Node-graph-based static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
